Near the end of the return stroke, the follower pin opens a normally closed flush poppet connected to the flush bypass. 1	Many liquid handling installations add a small, accurately measured quantity of a concentrate to a much larger stream of a carrier liquid that is already flowing in a pipe. The concentrate may be aggressive, staining, strongly colored, biologically active, or simply expensive, and the quantity that must be added is small in comparison with the carrier flow. The addition therefore has to be made repeatably, without measuring the concentrate by eye, and without allowing the concentrate to reach any part of the installation other than the carrier stream itself.
2	
3	Two practical difficulties dominate this kind of dosing. The first is separation of the two liquids upstream of the point of addition. A dosing device sits between a concentrate source and a pressurized carrier line, and any path that momentarily connects the two allows carrier liquid to be forced back into the concentrate source or allows concentrate to migrate into the carrier line at a time when no dose is called for. Where the two sides are kept apart by separately actuated shut-off elements, the separation depends on those elements being commanded in the correct order.
4	
5	The second difficulty is residue. The surfaces that the concentrate touches, in particular the port through which it enters the metering volume and the seat of the check element through which the dose leaves, may retain a film of concentrate after the dose has been delivered. Where such a film passes into the carrier stream between doses, the quantity actually added is not the quantity that was measured; and where it dries or reacts on the wetted surfaces, the accuracy of the valve changes in service. Where the valve must be broken out of the line and cleaned by hand, the installation is taken out of service; and where a rinse is a separate operation commanded after the dose, it depends on that operation being performed at the right moment.
6	
7	Dose selection presents a further difficulty. Adjustable dosing devices may be set by a screw or by an electronically stored value. There remains a need for a setting that is retained by the mechanism itself and that is visible at the valve without electronics.
8	
9	There remains a need for an inline metering valve in which the separation of the concentrate from the carrier liquid is enforced by the geometry of the moving parts rather than by the order in which external commands arrive, in which the surfaces wetted by the concentrate are rinsed by the carrier liquid as an unavoidable part of the return of the metering element, and in which the selected dose is both retained and displayed mechanically.

findings.title: Background asserts a backflow/migration hazard and a pressurized carrier line as unconditional fact, unsupported by any source in the workspace
findings.detail: prior_art/INDEX.md lists no references and the draft carries no [REF:] citation, so nothing in the workspace supports a statement of fact about how existing dosing installations behave. input/disclosure.md and input/conversation.md say only that "The ordering of the port edges and lands prevents the concentrate source from communicating directly with the carrier-liquid inlet"; they say nothing about the carrier line being pressurized, about carrier liquid being forced back into the concentrate source, or about concentrate migrating into the carrier line between doses. The remainder of the section is already written as conditional need-framing ("Where the two sides are kept apart by separately actuated shut-off elements...", "Where such a film passes into the carrier stream between doses...", "Adjustable dosing devices may be set by a screw or by an electronically stored value"), so this sentence is now the section's only unconditional assertion of fact about existing practice, and assertions of that kind in a background can be read as applicant admissions. I mark it minor because it is problem framing rather than a statement about the invention, and the need it frames - geometric separation of the two liquids - is squarely disclosed.
